findings.evidence: Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there until the payment clears.
findings.fix: Name the manager explicitly as the subject of the countersigning sentence, or move that instruction to a section written for the manager, so the paragraph's 'you' keeps referring to one reader throughout.
findings.violation: The paragraph addresses the reader directly as 'you' for submitting and tracking the request, then inserts an imperative, 'Countersign the employee request,' whose implied actor is a manager rather than the employee, with no signal marking that the instruction's audience has changed, so a reader cannot tell whether that sentence is theirs to act on.

findings.evidence: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review.
findings.fix: Pick one term for the object being recorded, reconciled, and paid, and use it in all three sentences.
findings.violation: Three consecutive sentences name the thing moving through the request pipeline with three different terms (stipend item, reimbursable item, covered purchase), with no defined-terms signal that they mean the same thing, so the reader cannot tell whether one object is being tracked through three stages or three different things are being described.

findings.evidence: Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing. The employee receives a confirmation email once processing finishes. Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request.
findings.fix: Reorder this section into the employee's actual step sequence: submit the request, review the confirmation summary, then describe the manager/finance/processing steps that happen after submission.
findings.violation: The section narrates the manager's sign-off, finance's budget confirmation, final processing, and a confirmation email as already complete, and only afterward tells the employee to review a summary before submitting the final request, so the reader cannot reconstruct the actual order of their own steps without re-reading and guessing which 'request' is which.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout.
findings.fix: Rewrite the opening sentence to state the topic the rest of the paragraph covers.
findings.violation: The paragraph's opening sentence shares almost no vocabulary with the rest of the paragraph, so it does not preview the paragraph's actual topic.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.fix: Remove the travel-audit, federal-guidance, and coffee-budget sentences, or move each to a section where it is actually relevant; keep this section limited to how the benefits team coordinates stipend requests.
findings.violation: After its first sentence, the section moves through a travel-expense audit, remote-work federal guidance, and the office coffee budget, three themes unrelated to each other and to stipend coordination, with no signal connecting any of them, so a reader finishing the section cannot state what it was actually about.

findings.evidence: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review.
findings.fix: Keep one subject or a clearly signaled handoff between sentences, and refer to the tracked object by one consistent term across the three sentences.
findings.violation: The subject changes in every sentence (you, Finance, Payroll) and each sentence also introduces a new name for the object being acted on (stipend item, reimbursable item, covered purchase), with no sentence picking up the subject or term the previous sentence just established, so the reader has to re-orient at every sentence boundary instead of following one running topic.

findings.evidence: Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing.
findings.fix: Move the interrupting clause elsewhere, or split it into its own sentence.
findings.violation: 3 comma-set-off clause(s) totalling 14 words intervene between the sentence's apparent subject and its verb.

findings.evidence: An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The...
findings.fix: Open the paragraph with a transition word that states its relationship to the prior paragraph.
findings.violation: The paragraph opens with none of the fixed transition words, so the reader is not told how it relates to the paragraph before it.

findings.evidence: The stipend pays up to 500 dollars per benefit year. The finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle.
findings.fix: Name the finance office as the subject of the first sentence as well: 'The finance office pays up to 500 dollars per benefit year.'
findings.violation: The first sentence's subject is the stipend itself, an abstraction standing in for the finance office that actually pays, which the very next sentence names correctly as the one depositing the amount, so the document names the real actor inconsistently across two adjacent sentences describing the same payment.

findings.evidence: Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt.
findings.fix: Restate every item in the series with the same grammatical form.
findings.violation: The series' 2 items mix grammatical forms (gerund, other) at their head words instead of sharing one form.

findings.evidence: The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out.
findings.fix: Move the threshold to the end: 'Before paying out, the finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars.'
findings.violation: The sentence's newest and most consequential element, the 200-dollar review threshold, lands in the middle, and the sentence closes on 'before it pays out,' a detail the reader already expects and the section does not return to, so the stress position is spent on already-known context instead of the threshold the reader needs.
